feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overstuffed with overlapping skills sections, which reduces impact and scannability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization support leadership growth and domain depth.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics, e.g. “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong professional summary and consistent focus on digital strategy, governance, content operations, and mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in the freelance role and earlier NACo roles; include measurable results where possible.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation/list style is inconsistent (mix of commas, ampersands, slashes, and hyphen-led bullets embedded in paragraphs); “English (Native) French (A2/Learning)” needs separators for clarity. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, a more concise structure, and one or two concrete signals of scale or sector relevance.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and fix grammar: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with your current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leader for mission-driven, advocacy, and membership organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a more compact, executive-level framing.
- Add specificity tied to the CV, such as platform modernization, editorial systems, analytics, and translating policy issues for public-sector audiences.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, analytics, and multi-platform content operations. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear audience-focused messaging while aligning stakeholders, governance, and systems to support complex organizations.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize leadership-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe toward higher-value, differentiating capabilities: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder alignment • Advocacy & policy messaging • Multimedia production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and clearer ownership.
- Replace “Web & CMS administration” with “CMS modernization” or “Web platform strategy” to sound more strategic and current.
- Standardize style: use either all nouns or all noun phrases; avoid mixing functions (“coordination”) with outputs (“production”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo work. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Established,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable context where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Rephrase technically: “Built Drupal-based campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member resource hubs; improved CMS workflows, front-end delivery, and troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold specifics.
- Governance/workflows/analytics also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is newly owned or delivered in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team/operating leadership, and measurable business impact over channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise modernization for a 10,000+ page Drupal ecosystem.”
- Tighten and combine channel bullets: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with outcome-focused language tied to reach, engagement, or campaign performance if available.
- Strengthen impact phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for studio/analytics/governance work: cost savings, faster publishing, improved reporting adoption, reduced vendor reliance, or increased video output.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current email/social/video management language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may partially overlap with older video-production bullets; keep this focused on scale/capability, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcome language: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language—keep this item focused on hands-on management, not enterprise leadership.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting experience. It should be tightened to emphasize leadership scope and strategic value rather than restating generic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Make leadership clearer and more distinctive: “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel content operations and governance leadership.”
- Tighten for concision and consistency: “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and mission-driven messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple recent roles; keep only if phrased more distinctly.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search; move older/lower-priority platforms later or remove.
- Consider dropping either SharePoint or Power Pages unless they are important for target roles; they dilute the stronger public-sector web modernization story.
- If space allows, sharpen wording: replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based workflow systems” and “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full platform/tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “workflow automation” also overlap with Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize strategic use of analytics and avoid overlap with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill set to outcomes from NACo (analytics infrastructure expansion, improved decision-making) rather than listing more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool stack below.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps slightly with broader analytics/reporting language; consider consolidating to “SEO, UX and performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus tool detail in Technical + IT. Make it more senior, outcomes-oriented, and focused on capabilities most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Broadcast, Studio & Hybrid Event Production**

- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event delivery and technical run-of-show coordination
- If space allows, add one stronger qualifier such as **recurring advocacy programming** or **in-house studio buildout support** to reflect recent NACo work.
- Keep tool names (e.g., Premiere Pro) out of this section since they already appear under Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly redundant with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and several NACo bullets.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “livestream operations”; combine rather than list separately.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a simple platform list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider de-emphasizing older/lighter-use tools if space is tight.
- If accurate, add qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal 10**, **enterprise CMS administration**, **multi-publisher environments**, **public-sector web platforms**.
- Keep naming consistent: change **Power Pages** to **Microsoft Power Pages** for clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; consider trimming one or making this version more implementation-focused.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless it supports a specific portfolio or microsite use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Technical Implementation** to distinguish it from platform/CMS skills.
- Replace broad labels with sharper phrasing: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)**.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome cues in parentheses, e.g., **API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment automation)**.
- Consider dropping version numbers unless they matter; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner than **HTML5/CSS3**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary the framing.
- This item should avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress/AI-enabled search, which are already covered elsewhere more strategically.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Move collaboration tools out of this line unless they were used for automation/integration; Slack, Teams are better grouped under collaboration/productivity.
- If space allows, add light context: “for editorial planning, intake workflows, approvals, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider a stronger label: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” or “Automation, Intake & Work Management.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each is genuinely current/relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list rather than a capability statement. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth, not repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten the line to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for scope: **Campaign automation, newsletter operations, and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Keep vendor names consistent with the rest of the CV; use “Customer Insights/Journeys” only if that is the exact product naming you used professionally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in recent work experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider listing it first to better align with your most relevant experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list repetition: focus on website refresh, livestream/video production, and workflow support rather than “web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scale where possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, cadence of weekly updates, size/timing of website refresh, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day digital production workflows. Also provided informal supervision and task coordination for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on establishing the capability.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; use more junior, execution-level wording here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements—rather than repeats—the later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business value: supported program and policy teams through research, project coordination, and communications deliverables.
- Split into 2 concise bullets and emphasize ownership: planning, scripting, production, and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add scale or outcomes: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of multimedia/digital assets produced.

Suggested edit:
- Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, project coordination, and communications deliverables for program teams.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production while contributing digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that overlaps with the stronger 2015–2024 digital/media roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia here unless you can distinguish it from later weekly video and studio work.
